text:
dinesh: Heads up — our Jenkins canary deploy started failing this morning on the `deploy:canary` step with 403 from Redwood API: "insufficient_scope". Started after we rotated the Vault AppRole secret-id yesterday.

maya: Can you paste the exact error snippet and confirm this is Redwood Private (VPC) or hosted? Also share the pipeline step that obtains the token.

dinesh: Private (VPC). Error log:
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx...MASKED..." https://private-api.redwood.local/v1/models/list
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token expired or missing scopes"}
```
We mint tokens via Vault AppRole with TTL=60s. The canary step runs ~80–100s. There used to be an explicit token refresh in the Jenkinsfile but a housekeeping commit (c3f5a2) removed it.

jenkins-admin: Confirming Jenkins uses a shell step that runs: `vault write -format=json auth/approle/login role_id=$ROLE_ID secret_id=$SECRET_ID` and exports `REDFWOOD_TOKEN=$(jq -r .auth.client_token)`. The previous pipeline did a background reauth before long steps. Recent change removed the reauth stage.

liz: Short term fixes:
- Bump the AppRole token TTL to something safe (e.g., 600s) for the Jenkins role so in-flight jobs don't die. Command: `vault write auth/approle/role/jenkins token_ttl=600 token_max_ttl=1200`
- Re-add a refresh step in the Jenkinsfile to reacquire token if step > token TTL. Example snippet: 
```sh
TOKEN_OBTAINED=$(date +%s)
TTL=60  # replace with actual TTL/pulled meta
# before long-running step
if [ $(( $(date +%s) - TOKEN_OBTAINED )) -gt $((TTL - 10)) ]; then
  REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(vault write -field=client_token auth/approle/login role_id=$ROLE_ID secret_id=$SECRET_ID)
fi
```
Longer term: add client-side TTL detection & auto-refresh in the canonical Jenkins shared library.

dinesh: Ok I can hotfix: bump TTL to 600 and reinsert refresh. Is there any risk making the TTL longer for that role? We rely on frequent secret-id rotation for safety.

maya: Longer TTL is ok short-term if you restrict the role's permissions tightly (least-privilege) and enable audit logging. Also consider an alternate approach: create a CI-dedicated Redwood service account with a non-ephemeral token scoped only to canary deploy (read-only lists + deploy endpoints) and audit key usage — use that as a fallback while we fix the pipeline. If you want support escalation on Redwood side, I can pull logs for token rejection traces (include token fingerprint) and open an eng ticket.

vault-bot: secret-id rotated for approle "jenkins" at 2026-03-15T22:03:10Z

jenkins-admin: Will push the Jenkinsfile change (add refresh + write build log on token acquired) and revert the accidental commit. Pushing now, will run a canary.

dinesh: Patch deployed, canary started. If this fails again I'll attach full pipeline trace. Thanks :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — keep me posted. If you still see 403s after refresh/TLL bump I'll escalate to eng-runtime for a deeper trace on the auth validation path.
